question: Should durable plugin `allow-always` approvals become a core plugin API now, and should Skill Workshop opt into it in this PR?
rationale: This changes a plugin author contract and a persistent approval security boundary; automation can identify the current defects, but maintainers need to own the final trust model and API shape.

options.title: Fix Skill Workshop scope before merge
options.body: Add a stable core/plugin owner, replace the request-visible workspace path with a non-sensitive stable scope, preserve current-main routing fields during rebase, and prove a second matching lifecycle request reuses `allow-always`.

options.title: Split the built-in opt-in out
options.body: Land only the generic persistence mechanism after API review and keep Skill Workshop lifecycle approvals on `allow-once`/`deny` until its owner and audit model are ready.

options.title: Accept the API direction explicitly
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the expanded plugin API and persistent trust boundary after documenting upgrade behavior, key visibility, retention, and operator expectations.

recommendation.title: Fix Skill Workshop scope before merge
recommendation.body: Add a stable core/plugin owner, replace the request-visible workspace path with a non-sensitive stable scope, preserve current-main routing fields during rebase, and prove a second matching lifecycle request reuses `allow-always`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the plugin approval framework and gateway/plugin API contract that this branch expands.
